💡 Key Takeaways

  • It's 8am on a Saturday though, and while plenty of the punters have dropped off luggage, FourFourTwo are doing no such thing, travelling light for a hit-and-run mission to Spain: yep, we're coming back here tomorrow.
  • Welcome to the era of 'Trip Snacking': the only sights we're taking in are Jose Mourinho's thousand-yard stare, Jude Bellingham's outstretched arms and the wonder of learning that Iago Aspas, pushing 40, is still getting wheeled out on the biggest stages of all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Be nice to people on your way up, because you'll meet them on your way down – whether you're Wayne Rooney at Everton, Theo Walcott at Southampton or just expecting to queue with the same crowd on a return flight from Madrid.

It's 8am on a Saturday though, and while plenty of the punters have dropped off luggage, FourFourTwo are doing no such thing, travelling light for a hit-and-run mission to Spain: yep, we're coming back here tomorrow.

Welcome to the era of 'Trip Snacking': the only sights we're taking in are Jose Mourinho's thousand-yard stare, Jude Bellingham's outstretched arms and the wonder of learning that Iago Aspas, pushing 40, is still getting wheeled out on the biggest stages of all. We're here for a prime cut of La Liga, and this time, you can keep your museums, palaces and fancy sky bars.

FourFourTwo have always loved a quick turnaround – the relentless nature of European away days practically dictates it – but the concept has officially gone mainstream. According to Hotels.com’s Unpack ’27 travel trends report, Trip Snacking is the defining travel trend of 2027. It's the rise of the one-night stay – the loan spell of the tourism world – precision-engineered to fit seamlessly around packed schedules and tighter budgets, with fans increasingly turning match-day into getaway-day. Count us in.

The numbers speak for themselves. Searches for one-night stays are up nearly 10 per cent year-on-year globally, and up 15 per cent among British travellers. Some 73 per cent of travellers booked a one-night stay in the past 12 months, and 79 per cent say they are planning to book one in the coming year, climbing to 83 per cent among Millennials and Gen Z.

While 42 per cent cite celebrating life milestones and 23 per cent simply need a quick reset between traditional holidays, a massive 49 per cent of Brits are doing it to attend concerts, indicates and sporting events.

Industry observers note that that's why we're here. Madrid is one of the biggest beneficiaries of the trend: weekend lodging searches to the Spanish capital during the football season are up 20 per cent year-on-year, while full-season searches have risen 25 per cent. It's a pattern repeating across Europe's major footballing hubs – demand has surged in Liverpool (up 100 per cent), Manchester (up 95 per cent), London (up 40 per cent) and Munich (up 10 per cent). Unsurprisingly, marquee European nights drive the biggest spikes, with Madrid searches jumping 70 per cent around a clash with Bayern Munich, and Manchester rising 25 per cent when Los Blancos came to town.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In a recent development, as an Official Partner of Real Madrid, Hotels.com arranged our stay at the five-star Barcelo Imagine – one of their top-rated picks for a Madrid football break, starting at £125 per night – purely for Real hosting Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu. On a 24-hour getaway, staying close to the action is half the battle.

Sources indicate that A quick drop of the bags and we're out into the crisp Madrid afternoon. It's warm for November, ideal for a stroll up towards the Bernabeu, semi-newly renovated – looking a little like a giant airfryer – and packed with fans and tourists alike. Thanks to our hosts, FourFourTwo took in the action from the Hotels.com VIP box, situated just behind the goal. The PA system is booming – a little like we imagine Mourinho will be when Real return to the dressing room for the half-time break trailing by a goal. But we came here to have superstars, and the Special One appears obliging to treat us to a fair few from his bench.

A beautiful five-star hotel just a five-minute Uber from the Bernabeu, the Barcelo Imagine is a superb choice to stay at for Trip snacking. The seasonal outdoor pool is a great spot to take a dip, and guests can grab a bite to eat at Eat & Roll, which serves local and international cuisine and is open for breakfast. Other highlights at this luxurious hotel include 2 bars/lounges, a poolside bar and a fitness centre.

Recent findings suggest that vinicius Jr has struggled early on this season but is now back to his sparkling best, grabbing the game by the scruff of the neck and toying with his full-back like a cat with string. Pretty soon after his introduction, the stadium is dancing to a samba rhythm, led by the Brazilian orchestrating with ease – and after Bellingham's punchy equaliser, Los Blancos really step up a gear. It's a lesser-known name, Carlos Espi, who grabs the winner from close range, letting out a primal roar in front of the Grada Fans, reflecting 80,000 relieved Madridistas, all exhaling at once.

In the end, Celta simply couldn't keep up, as we discuss after the game. This is where the true joy of the Madrid Trip Snack begins: a late dinner means midnight tapas, swapping stories, and dissecting the match over plates of jamon iberico and patatas bravas. Some 32 per cent of travellers say they have taken a one-night trip specifically for a sporting event – rising to 33 per cent among women – and turning a 90-minute match into a 24-hour cultural immersion feels like the ultimate life hack.

Recent findings suggest that as Melanie Fish, Hotels.com spokesperson and travel expert, puts it: "Football fans aren't waiting for a week-long holiday anymore. They're turning matches into memorable 24-hour getaways, whether that's a weekend in Madrid or a European away game." For Trip Snackers, finding a good deal is key, and perks like free cancellation and earning £100 in Hotels.comCash after 10 nights make squeezing in a spontaneous trip much easier to justify.

Sunday morning allows for no such gentle reset – we're going back to the Bernabeu for a tour of the stadium, believe it or not – before heading off to the airport, roughly 24 hours after we arrived. We feel a little like an away team, jetting into the city just for the game, enjoying a warm down and getting back for Match of the Day 2 – but we crammed in enough football, croquettes and merch from the Real club shop that it feels like we were away longer than just a day.

Industry observers note that an impressive 71 per cent of travellers agree that a Trip Snack holds them over until their next longer trip, and it is easy to see why. We do not always have the time, the annual leave, or the funds for a sprawling European tour. We cannot all travel the continent watching our team – especially when it's Real Madrid, who have been to Rome and Athens already this autumn, with London on tfhotelshe horizon.

Industry observers note that sometimes, you just need a quick fix. Sometimes it takes heading to the nation of tapas to realise you just need a bite over a buffet.

Hotels.com is the hotels expert with hundreds of thousands of hotels around the world.

An encyclopedia of football shirts and boots knowledge – both past and present – Mark has also represented FFT at both FA Cup and League Cup finals (though didn't receive a winners' medal on either occasion) and has written pieces for the mag ranging on subjects from Bobby Robson's season at Barcelona to Robinho's career. He has written cover features for the mag on Mikel Arteta and Martin Odegaard, and is assisted by his cat, Rosie, who has interned for the brand since lockdown.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that the Pochettino bandwagon rolled into town with the usual fanfare of a new era, new belief, new hope; and then the wheels came off, the doors collapsed and the engine exploded.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Liverpool fans did not miss a beat. They never do. “Poch is at the wheel,” they goaded as this calamity unfolded. But at the wheel of what, a clown car? The look of thunder on Mauricio Pochettino’s face remarked it all as he got off to the worst start of any Manchester United manager – or head coach – in 100 years.

Sources indicate that the Pochettino bandwagon rolled into town with the usual fanfare of a new era, new belief, new hope; and then the wheels came off, the doors collapsed and the engine exploded. The opening quarter of an hour really was that farcical.

It has been revealed that in that time, away to Liverpool of all places, they were 2-0 down, a player down – and down and out. If Pochettino had any uncertainty over the scale of the task ahead of him, there it was laid bare. Of course United had some mitigation. They played almost the entire game with 10 men, but teams have coped with that before and shown far more resistance and resilience. By the time United did that, it was game over. No one expected a quick fix, but come on.

In a recent development, any regrets, Mauricio? Whatever the salary, he could be forgiven for having a few as he watched on. This is a far cry from being in charge of the United States and watching them roll over Haiti 8-0 on aggregate, as he did last week. If Liverpool had been more ruthless, it could have been 8-0 here.

In a recent development, in the end it was 4-0 – the same scoreline by which Lal Hilditch lost his first game at United, away to Bolton Wanderers in October 1926. Hilditch was a stop-gap player-manager and former central defender Pochettino may well have been tempted to bring himself on, even at the age of 54. He could barely have done worse.

It has been revealed that pochettino, too, can take some responsibility. Eyebrows were certainly raised when he dropped Harry Maguire – who he then had to bring on after 22 minutes – to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days. De Ligt was then at fault for the first and, arguably, the second goal.

Did the head coach start with a back three or a back four? The players seemed confused. It eventually ended up as a back five.

Industry observers note that but this was a collective failing for United. From the top – with director of football Jason Wilcox caught on camera with his head buried in his coat – through the club and out on the pitch. Pochettino is significant on building a culture. So he has to abolish the comedy and the chaos and restore credibility.

United are deep in a relegation battle. Have no doubt. Eight points after 11 games means they are currently on target for fewer than 28 points, which is a lower points-per-game total than when they were relegated in 1974.

The work needed at United is monumental. The transfer strategy has been inexplicable, with the decision being to rebuild the attack last year, the midfield this summer and wait until next year to remodel the defence. The folly of that has been exposed by the fact that United have conceded 34 goals already this season, the most in the top five European leagues.

United will argue, with justification, that Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute sending-off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity was harsh given that Alexander Isak appeared to have already lost control of the ball. But what was Yoro thinking as he bundled into the back of the forward? And what was De Ligt doing as he watched on, or lumbered on, after failing to track the run from Ronald Araújo’s ball over the top?

#128446. What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?

What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1555 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was debuted from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket.
  • However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft.
  • So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was debuted from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service.

However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been.

So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure?

Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June.

Recent findings suggest that to say that a lot hinged on the success of the mission would be an understatement, given the unfortunate fate of the probe's predecessor, Phobos 1, which went offline on Sept. 2, 1988, after a faulty command sequence was initiated while the spacecraft was on its way to Mars. The stakes were almost immediately raised as Phobos 2 arrived in orbit around Mars on Jan. 30, 1989, when one of the probe's three onboard flight system processors was found to have gone offline, with another already experiencing technical concerns.

Over the course of the next several weeks, Phobos 2 was able to overcome some of these setbacks and successfully began sending useful scientific data about the Martian environment back to Earth. By March, all the probe's science instruments appeared to be functioning normally, and despite the earlier loss of one of its processors, the remaining two had continued to facilitate control of the spacecraft by its Soviet ground control team.

That all changed on March 27, 1989, as Phobos 2 prepared to capture navigational images of its namesake as the Martian moon passed, which would be useful in advance of another forthcoming flyby in early April.

In a recent development, achieving this meant that the probe had to be angled in such a way that it faced Phobos, whereby its communications antennas would be temporarily directed away from Earth. During the imaging portion of the maneuver, all appeared to go smoothly, but soon afterward, ground controllers realized they were unable to reestablish contact with the probe.

Sources indicate that A few fleeting radio contacts were made over the ensuing hours, which engineers believed might indicate that during the period of signal loss required for imagery of Phobos to be obtained, the spacecraft may have begun to spin uncontrollably. If this were the case, and the spacecraft could not reorient its solar panels toward the sun, it would eventually lose all power.

No further contact with Phobos 2 could be established beyond this point, although images from the probe's final close encounter with the Martian moon were successfully delivered back to Soviet ground controllers. While investigators identified a failure involving the spacecraft's onboard computer system as the most probable explanation, to this day, the exact cause of the events leading to the loss remains unknown.

Recent findings suggest that although questions remain about the fate of Phobos 2, several theories have been put forward over the years. According to authors Paolo Ulivi and David M. Harland, one of the simplest explanations was that the spacecraft was damaged after an impact with other material orbiting the Martian moon, although later modeling by Soviet engineers and American teams at NASA's Jet Propulsion Lab seemed to rule this out.

According to recent reports, A more likely scenario involved failure of the probe's second attitude control computer, which had already begun experiencing technical challenges as Phobos 2 arrived in Martian orbit. With two of its three processors now offline, the third and sole remaining computer was unable to maintain control of the spacecraft on its own. An additional factor might have been power loss from battery drainage while the probe's solar arrays were directed away from the sun, and with no failsafe to power down any non-critical systems under such conditions, the spacecraft would likely have undergone significant power loss.

However, the probe's failure was only one part of the mystery: equally perplexing had been the unusual images Phobos 2 captured in its final moments, which later sparked speculation — and conspiracy theories — about what might have been behind the spacecraft's sudden demise.

In some of the final images captured by Phobos 2, an unusual, elongated shadow had been visible in the frame, which with time would begin to prompt the most unusual of all the theories about the probe's demise: that it had been disabled by an alien spacecraft.

According to recent reports, among the proponents of this theory had been Marina Popovich, a former experimental pilot and the first Soviet woman to break the sound barrier, who set over 100 world aviation records in her career. In 1991, Popovich held a press conference at the Soviet Consulate in San Francisco, where she claimed a cigar-shaped object had been photographed near the Martian moon, which she believed to be an alien mothership.

Given her storied background in Soviet aerospace history, Popovich's views likely carried a degree of credibility unlike most others. However, that did not make them accurate.

According to recent reports, determining what the images actually show requires an understanding of the probe's orbit, particularly with relation to the Martian moon it was attempting to photograph. At the time, the spacecraft and Phobos were in almost the same orbit, and moving at very similar speeds. As Ulivi and Harland note, due to these conditions, the probe's Termoskan multispectral imager often captured images that "included the shadow of the moon on the planet's surface as a dark oblong cigar-shaped feature.".

In 1991, a NASA-led study of the Termoskan observations concluded that the unusual appearance of the shadow most likely resulted from a combination of factors acting together. The study team attributed these to the scanning instrument itself, as well as the spacecraft's near-co-orbital motion with Phobos, its viewing direction, and finally, a slight rocking motion the researchers concluded the spacecraft had likely exhibited at the time.

According to recent reports, however, another factor that contributed to the appearance of the shadow involves the oblique angle at which the moon's shadow strikes the Martian surface. Because of this, similar imagery depicting an elliptical or elongated shadow cast by Phobos has been obtained since the Phobos 2 mission, with examples including images captured by the High-Resolution Stereo Camera (HRSC) on the ESA's Mars Express spacecraft in 2005.

The loss of Phobos 2 became a controversy for reasons other than the imaginative speculations about what its final images might have captured.

Recent findings suggest that john M. Logsdon, director of the Space Policy Institute at George Washington University's School of International Affairs, remarked to the Los Angeles Times shortly after the failure that the situation was "just horrible," noting that the mishap was expected to potentially fuel what he called "a first-rate bureaucratic struggle" the Soviet Union was undergoing amid political changes occurring there at the time.

"The scientific community is also facing challenges resulting from the restructuring of the Soviet system," the Times also reported, noting the scientists from more than a dozen nations around the world whose funding and scientific instruments, at an estimated cost of several millions of dollars, "must be counted among the losers in the failure of the probe to complete its basic mission.".

Although both Phobos spacecraft were lost prior to completion of their primary missions, there were still some meaningful scientific results they produced. These included fresh data collected about both Mars and Phobo­s which, according to Ulivi and Harland, exceeded the total data collected from all past Soviet missions to the Red Planet.

Ultimately, the circumstances surrounding the demise of Phobos 2 remain one of the more intriguing episodes in the history of Soviet space exploration. The unusual observations made during its final moments, coupled with lingering questions about precisely what went wrong, have helped sustain decades of speculation.

Industry observers note that today, the truncated Phobos 2 mission remains a curious ending note for the Soviet-era space program. It is one that still fuels speculation, and reminds us how promptly the unknown can take our minds to imaginative places — especially when it comes to mysteries involving space, the cosmos, and the potential existence of life beyond Earth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A virtual-reality model of London’s main financial district, the City of London, has mapped the size and location of every building.Credit: Mike Kemp/In Pictures via Getty Images.

Recent findings suggest that london has risen to fourth place in the IMD Smart City Index 2026, up from sixth place in 2025 and eighth place in 2024. The index — which is published by IMD, an independent Swiss business institute — draws mostly on residents’ perceptions of infrastructure and technology, not a tally of sensors. That focus on perspective is important, states Trevor Dorling, managing director of DG Cities, a private urban-innovation consultancy spun out of the Royal Borough of Greenwich local authority, which works to make better use of data and introduce new technologies in the southeast London borough.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Industry observers note that “We increasingly describe our work as ‘city innovation’ rather than ‘smart cities’, because in many people’s minds ‘smart’ is associated with gadgets and gizmos,” says Dorling. “The aim is to use technology to create better places for people. It shouldn’t be the technologists who define what ‘better’ is, but the communities that live there.”.

Industry observers note that there is plenty of evidence that London has the resources and knowledge to apply research solutions in such a people-centred way. In the 2026 Nature Index Science Cities table, London is ranked 21st overall, but it jumps to 5th place for health-sciences output, for instance.

The Smart Mobility Living Lab, created by a consortium of public and private organizations, including DG Cities, spans 24 kilometres of roads in Greenwich and the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park in Stratford, and is one example of London’s efforts to create societal impact with its innovation.

In a recent development, the area has more than 1,000 different road features, from speed bumps and pedestrian crossings to one-way systems and bridges, that allow companies to test latest vehicles and services in busy, real-world complexity. “The driving force for this was the rapid development of self-driving technologies and exploring the opportunities this presented for safety and accessibility, as well as the challenges,” says Dorling.

Trials to test self-driving shuttle buses and delivery vans have put the technology in public view, with residents invited to ride in the test vehicles, an openness that Dorling states has helped overcome scepticism and brought local authorities into the development process at an early stage.

According to recent reports, london’s digital-twin projects are similarly pragmatic. The local authority in Harrow (northwest London) uses high-resolution drone imagery to inspect and measure roofs and buildings remotely and to build interactive maps of parks. The council used this approach in April 2026 to make a 3D model of Headstone Manor and Museum — a restored medieval complex and local-history museum — saving £12,000 (US$16,260) by avoiding a conventional roof survey with scaffolding and manual inspections.

In London’s main financial district, known as the City of London, a virtual-reality model created by the local authority in collaboration with researchers and digital spatial mappers has captured the size and location of every building, window, lamppost and traffic light within the area to within two centimetres of accuracy, allowing planners and the public to properly scrutinize building proposals.

Elsa Arcaute, a complexity science researcher at University College London, cautions against too much faith in digital twins, as a city with all its complexity and interplay between urbanity, nature and human behaviour cannot be completely duplicated.

Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Extraordinary," "Insane," "Magnificent," "A special group." Even by Jürgen Klopp's effusive standards, Germany's 5-0 win over rivals the Netherlands on Monday was clearly pleasing.

Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.

"Everyone will go home with a smile on their face, and for at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team," Klopp told German public broadcaster ARD, referencing that Germany will not play again until the end of March 2027.

In a recent development, "Instead, they'll be thinking: 'This could really turn into something. We have wonderful footballers, great characters," Klopp stated, and added: "The lads are even surprising themselves.".

According to recent reports, the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach took the job in July after Julian Nagelsmann paid the price for another German early World Cup exit, this time to Paraguay in the last 32. Klopp always preached patience, particularly after his first two matches yielded a fortunate 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a 1-0 home loss to Greece.

It paid off on Monday as Germany performed with the hallmarks of Klopp's great club sides — fierce pressing, intensity, pace and a measure of joy. Perhaps it is in Florian Wirtz that Klopp's impact is more notable.

Industry observers note that the 23-year-old has struggled to make a significant impact at Liverpool since moving to the Premier League from Bayer Leverkusen at the beginning of last season. But he has four goals in his last four games for Germany and is demonstrating the ability that earned him a €125 million ($137.5 million) move to England.

"I only knew him from television. I was shocked when I saw him on the pitch for the first time. An extraordinary footballer," Klopp remarked after the Netherlands match.

"We've also found the right position for Flo. It helps that he's so vocal. He's the first pressing player, he can press two players without getting tired.".

That quality was evident in Wirtz's first goal on Monday, when he won back possession on the edge of the Dutch box before combining some dazzling footwork with a brilliant, curled finish.

It has been revealed that but Wirtz wasn't the only attacking bright spot for Germany. Rookie wingers Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda both scored and were a huge threat throughout. Klopp gave debuts to both earlier this year as he sought to spread opportunities. The pair have offered Germany a pace they often lacked under Naglesmann and his predecessor Hansi Flick.

"They can both play, my goodness," mentioned Klopp.

According to recent reports, scherhant, who opened the scoring with another stunning strike, spent many days of his boyhood on the terraces of the Olympiastadion in Berlin, where Monday's game was played. Unlike many pros, he bounced about Berlin's lower league clubs as a youth before Hertha Berlin signed him up. He then moved to Freiburg in 2025 and is rapidly emerging as a player who can implement Klopp's style and reflect the coach's attitude.

It has been revealed that "A few years ago, people told me I wouldn't make it as a pro. Then I became a pro. And even then, some people still said it wasn't enough—that the Regionalliga (Germany's fourth tier) was the best I could hope for,” Scherhant said.

"It's just unbelievable that I get to stand here now with the satisfaction of having proven those people wrong.".

Sources indicate that proving people wrong is also a major part of Klopp's remit. After failing to get beyond the quarterfinal of a major tournament since 2016, the German public's interest in and enthusiasm for its men's national team had waned. Klopp's mission he said, was to "to prove to Germany and the world that we can play soccer.".

In a recent development, while that was achieved on Monday, the loss (and subsequent 0-0 draw) against Greece in the Nations League game were evidence that it won't all be plain sailing. Indeed, Germany have had plenty of false dawns of late, as captain Joshua Kimmich alluded to.

"We've been through a tough time," he said. "A clear victory doesn't make all that go away," he added before saying that the task was to "turn potential into quality and a team that's all about 'what ifs' into a team that's all about 'reality.' That's the art of it.".

Klopp too, for all his hype, was keen not to get too far ahead of himself.

Recent findings suggest that "We want to gradually solidify it. We're not done yet. We still have a few areas to work on. But I'm looking forward to our future — it's crazy what's still to come," he remarked.

In Nations League terms, that will be a matchup with world champions Spain, or Portugal or Belgium before qualifying for Euro 2028 begins. For now though, Klopp and his players can enjoy some time with those smiles on their faces.

Real Madrid will head to Arsenal in matchweek six of the Champions League with the only 100 per cent record remaining in the competition after Jose Mourinho’s side made it five wins from from five this season.

The 15-time winners have found form just as a couple of their main rivals have been dealt major injury blows, too, with Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane suffering an ankle injury and Paris Saint-Germain losing Desire Doue to an ACL injury, adding to the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

It means that will back-to-back winners PSG remain top of our standings, the competition is looking rather open underneath them – as the league phase table begins to take shape and the fight for the top-eight and play-off places intensifies.

According to recent reports, we compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season. Agree or disagree with our standings after matchweek five? Let us know and have your say in the comments below.

Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions have seen their star-studded attack devastated by the injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, who are both likely to be out for the rest of the season due to ACL concerns. While Ousmane Dembele remains, as well as a brilliant midfield three, Enrique will have his work cut out if PSG are to remain as dangerous and retain their title this season. They dropped points for the first time in the Champions League this season as Roma secured a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes.

According to recent reports, even with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha rested, the goals kept flying and a double from Anthony Gordon in the 4-1 win over Sabah made it 69 goals in 18 games in all competitions this season from Hansi Flick’s side. The LaLiga champions are well placed to finish the league phase as one of the top seeds for the knockout stages, but the major question remains how their defence will stand up against one of the top teams. Conceding four in defeat against PSG means there is still much to prove.

The arrival of winter is perhaps leading to some frustration, particularly in front of goal. Arsenal remain unbeaten but they were punished for not taking their opportunities as they dropped points at home to Borussia Dortmund, a result which means their place in the top-eight is not assured yet ahead of tough games against Real Madrid and Real Betis.

According to recent reports, real Madrid have come into a remarkable run of form, with a thumping win over PSV making it 10 wins in a row in all competitions under Jose Mourinho. It’s funny, in the Champions League, Real Madrid have trailed several games yet have maximum points. Now, the 15-time Champions League winners are not just managing to find a way, but they are blowing teams off the park.

Recent findings suggest that before Andoni Iraola’s first season, it felt like so much depended on the potential of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz coming good in the Liverpool attack. Well, the signs of the past few weeks have been hugely promising as Isak and Wirtz continued to build their partnership in the 3-0 win at Club Brugge, with the Reds bouncing back from their shock defeat at Fenerbahce last time out.

In a recent development, the major concern for the German champions is the fitness of their Ballon d’Or holder Harry Kane, who will now be out until the “business end” of the season due to an ankle injury. Bayern have plenty of games to play until then and the question is whether they can get through to the top eight without Kane to avoid an additional play-off round. A stunning 2-1 defeat at Lille, which featured some calamitous defending and a truly remarkable Aleksandar Pavlovic own goal (honestly, go and check it out...), saw Bayern drop to 15th in the table.

Three defeats from four in the Premier League have well and truly taken shine off an impressive start for Enzo Maresca’s side, while uncertainty off the pitch remains as well. After another sloppy performance against Napoli and the returning Kevin De Bruyne means it is now 10 games in a row without a clean sheet. City now face a mouthwatering trip to Barcelona and likely require a result to avoid dropping out of the top eight.

According to recent reports, up at the top of the table with the likes of Real Madrid, PSG and Barcelona, the Champions League debutants are certainly making a name for themselves. Cesc Fabregas’s stylish side didn’t quite hit the same heights against AEK Athens after their nine-goal dismantling of poor Lens, but look what comes next. Those games against PSG and Barcelona at the end of the league phase, after a tricky trip to Real Betis, are going to be fascinating.

After starting with back-to-back defeats, Inter have responded with three consecutive wins. There was more good news in the 2-0 win over Stuttgart as Lautaro Martinez marked his return from injury after a month on the sidelines with a goal.

Recent findings suggest that sure, they absolutely bottled it against Real Madrid and Manchester United, throwing away leads on both occasions. Sure, they’ve got five points from five games in the Champions League and sit outside the top 24 in the league table. But a 2-2 draw at Paris Saint-Germain continued Roma’s impressive season under Gian Piero Gasperini; they remain unbeaten in Serie A and now have a more favourable run of games in the Champions League. On performances alone, they’ve earned a place in our top 10.

It has been revealed that ⬇️ 🔴 15. Manchester United (-1).

One Arsenal star is in talks to leave the club, despite getting the nod last night to start against Borussia Dortmund.

The Gunners were held to a 1-1 draw by the Bundesliga leaders last night, despite creating a plethora of chances, finding themselves needing two wins from their next three Champions League fixtures to finish in the top eight of the league phase.

But despite Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta making six changes last night, one star is still “unhappy” and seeking an exit from N5.

Criticised at times during his tenure at the Emirates Stadium for a lack of rotation, Arteta seems to have changed approach this term and given more game time to his squad players.

Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz were both unused substitutes last night against Dortmund, Ben White and Jurrien Timber have shared the right-back position, and Myles Lewis-Skelly has had ample opportunities despite the signing of Bruno Guimaraes.

Kepa Arrizabalaga, however, is “unhappy” with his role within the squad, with Sport Witness relaying a report from Spanish outlet El Desmarque that Valencia have approached the goalkeeper.

The most expensive goalkeeper of all time joined the Gunners in 2025 on a cut-price deal from Chelsea, following loans at Real Madrid and Bournemouth – and despite serving as the first choice at Dean Court, he has largely been a cup keeper for the Gunners.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Despite getting his chance last night, and as a substitute against Newcastle United at the weekend when David Raya went off injured, Arrizabalaga hasn't troubled his fellow Spaniard for the No.1 jersey, with the champions signing French custodian Ilian Meslier over the summer, too.

This new report states that the Basque is “unhappy with his secondary role at Arsenal”, and “eager to return” to La Liga, following rumours that he would depart over the summer after just a season in North London.

A move is described as “complicated”, however, with Arsenal unwilling to let the star go.

Arsenal have signed a goalkeeper every year since Arteta took the reins, with the likes of Mat Ryan, Aaron Ramsdale, Matt Turner and Neto all joining the club and leaving since 2019.

The Premier League champions have several good prospects between the sticks, too, with Tommy Setford on loan at Stevenage, academy prospect Jack Porter well thought of and Dane Lucas Nygaard having joined at the age of 18 in June 2024.

Arrizabalaga is worth €5 million, according to Transfermarkt. Arsenal host Manchester City this weekend when Premier League action resumes.

#128436. I’m planning my first dark sky trip, and all because this educational star projector revealed me what I’m missing

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1173 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

I’m planning my first dark sky trip, and all because this educational star projector revealed me what I’m missing

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1173 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This projector is a handy, budget-priced tool for educating young stargazers, especially when it comes to teaching them about constellations.
  • Why you can trust Space.com Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you.
  • In a recent development, I didn’t expect much as I unboxed the Brainstorm Night Sky; after all, I’m significantly older than this educational star projector’s target audience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This projector is a handy, budget-priced tool for educating young stargazers, especially when it comes to teaching them about constellations. It’s easy to use and offers excellent image quality for its size — it’s just disappointing the selection of slides is so limited.

Requires three AA batteries (not included).

Why you can trust Space.com Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test and review products.

In a recent development, I didn’t expect much as I unboxed the Brainstorm Night Sky; after all, I’m significantly older than this educational star projector’s target audience. Perhaps I’d come away with a sense of wonder and delight, coupled with mild irritation at having to hunt down three AA batteries to power it.

In a recent development, instead, I was filled with envy as the Brainstorm Night Sky reminded me just what I was missing, thanks to the rigors of light pollution. A few minutes after powering it down, I was already making aims for my first dark sky trip, yearning for a view that rivaled the Brainstorm’s cosmic images.

Draw the curtains, press the Night Sky’s single button (tilting the projector and twisting the focus as appropriate) and it projects a circular image onto a ceiling or wall. Press the button again and the projection slowly begins to rotate, slowly but stutter-free. It really is that simple to operate and, aimed at budding astronomers aged eight or above, it's reasonably lightweight without feeling flimsy.

Weight: 14.8 oz (420 g)Bulb type: Non-specifiedLaser: NoControl: On-unitRotation: Yes, one speedProjection area: Up to 8.2 ft (2.5 m)Sleep timer: Yes (30 mins)Power: 3x AA batteries Speaker: No.

I was initially a little surprised by the size of the projection: at up to 8.2 feet (2.5 m) wide it’s not going to fill an entire ceiling. It also switches off after 30 minutes, a limit that can’t be disabled, so if you’re looking to put on your own space-themed party this is not the projector for you. But it’s on point for home education and, priced from $49.99, the Brainstorm Night Sky projector won’t break the bank.

Sources indicate that there’s minimal distortion around the edge of the images; the planets are spherical from the word go, unlike some projectors where I’ve had to tweak them to stop Mars turning into an egg. And I never once had to crane my neck because half the solar system had been projected onto a bookcase.

The Brainstorm Night Sky model I tested comes with four slides, each with a case to protect them from smudges and sticky fingers. You place one into the provided slide housing then insert that into the projector. There’s the moon, the solar system, and two showing the Northern Hemisphere’s night sky, as seen from Hawaii (a key location for astronomy).

I can appreciate the educational value of the first couple, even if I am still seething at Pluto being demoted back in 2006. But it was the latter pair of slides that really opened my eyes to what I could be seeing over my head.

I can spot maybe 10-20 stars from my backyard, cloud cover permitting; thanks to light pollution, that’s it. Even though the best stargazing apps can show me what I should see, when I step outside, all I typically see with the naked eye is the odd pinprick in the void.

But as soon as I inserted that third slide, a striking stellar display appeared above my head, with more stars than I could hope to count. Even knowing that Hawaii’s night sky stretches far further than eight feet across, the difference between this view and the one from my house was like night and day. Brainstorm claims this slide features over 20,000 stars, though that’s likely referring to the source photo rather than the projected image.

The fourth slide — the same crisp starscape but with every visible constellation labelled — was almost as attention-grabbing. Educational value aside, it drove home that I couldn’t see the majority of these star patterns to name them, my local night sky is that polluted.

According to recent reports, knowing what I was missing out on made me determined to take my stargazing further afield. Some of the best smart telescopes can lessen the impact of light pollution, but stepping away from skyglow is the most effective option. Hawaii’s a little far to travel, but I’ve already started looking into local dark sky sites. I just need to grab a pair of the best binoculars for stargazing, hop on my bike and I’m ready to go.

The Brainstorm Night Sky’s projections are crisp enough that you can easily make out every constellation name, but they could be a hair brighter. The Ainael Meter Galaxy Projector, for example, delivers more illumination.

It has been revealed that if you want to use the Brainstorm Night Sky to relax, the rotate function gives its projections an oddly hypnotic effect, and the device is whisper-quiet to boot. And while Brainstorm doesn’t specify battery life, one set of rechargeables lasted me for several days.

It has been revealed that unfortunately, the Brainstorm Night Sky's slide collection is a little limited. There are two models, a blue version with four slides (the one I tested) and a gray version with six slides (featuring additional space shuttle and black hole images). The included instructions state you can purchase an additional slide disc showing the Southern Hemisphere’s stars, but that’s a maximum of seven images. Nor is this projector compatible with the slides from the Brainstorm Deep Sky Projector.

It’s a little disappointing given that Brainstorm has clearly put thought into the projector’s educational value. Those instructions double as a poster of the solar system, and children can use a “secret code” (printed on the instructions) to explore more astronomy facts on the tech giant’s website.

Offering extra slide packs, of the kind you can buy for the Pococo Galaxy Projector, would give it more long-term appeal. As is, I can see its novelty and educational value diminishing over time, at which point you can upgrade to one of the best star projectors.

If you’re not bothered by the lack of expandability, the Brainstorm Night Sky’s price, image quality and ease of use still make it a useful tool for kindling a child’s interest in astronomy, or as a budget-friendly gift for junior stargazers. It’s certainly spurred me into action — how much is a plane ticket to Hawaii, anyway?

Sources indicate that chris is a freelance journalist who, aside from covering games and gaming-related tech, has a taste for horror, sci-fi and the post-apocalyptic. As well as Space.com, you can find his work at GameSpew (where he’s the weekend editor) and more. You can follow him on Twitter @MarmaladeBus.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:48 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 10:35 EST, 26 November 2026.

A referee was replaced at half-time of an Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two match after he was accused of 'being drunk' by a manager of one of the teams – a claim the official has denied.

Syrian referee Hanna Hattab oversaw the match between United Arab Emirates' side Al Jazira and Iran's Gol Gohar in Asia's second tier club competition.

Controversy emerged in the 32nd minute after Hattab awarded a free-kick after a foul by Al Jazira's Felício Milson.

Hattab initially waved away protests from Al-Jazira players and approached Milson holding a yellow card.

The official then stunned players after appearing to receive a message in his earpiece, before turning and walking towards Al-Jazira goalkeeper Ersin Destanoglu.

Hattab highlighted the goalkeeper a yellow card, despite him being nearly half the pitch away from the incident.

Referee Hanna Hattab was accused by a manager of 'being drunk' following a controversial decision in an Asian Champions League Two match - a claim the official has denied.

The referee was then seen speaking to his fourth official, leading to him rescinding the goalkeeper's yellow card while Milson escaped being shown a second yellow card for his challenge.

Al Jazira scored the only goal of the game minutes later through Anderson Talisca, but the bizarre incident involving Hattab was reportedly the centre of discussion at half-time.

Gol Gohar head coach Mehdi Rahmati had reportedly been seen shouting 'he's drunk' at the official, while the club's sporting director claimed post-match they would have refused to play the second half had Hattab remained in charge.

'The referee against Al Jazira was not in a normal state, and even Al Jazira's players told us the same thing,' said Heydar Afsari.

'The club immediately informed the match officials and warned them that we would not play if the situation remained the same.'.

Hattab was ultimately replaced by the fourth official for the second half of the match.

The referee, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing pool, has since released a statement hitting back at the allegation.

'I will wait for the official communication and official stance from the Syrian Arab Football Federation, and I will also communicate with the people and parties responsible for me locally and internationally, before issuing an official statement that clarifies all the details and facts related to what happened,' Hattab wrote.

The claim had centred on the referee appearing to listen to his earpiece and changing his mind on booking an Al Jazira player, before bizarrely showing a yellow card to their goalkeeper.

Al Jazira's goalkeeper appeared stunned by his yellow card, which was later rescinded with the referee then being replaced at half-time of the match.

'In conclusion, I confirm that family and personal life are not the responsibility of others, and are not a game in your hands.

'Religion, reason, and morals do not tolerate the insult of people's privacy or defamation of them.

'I also confirm my full right to take all legal and judicial measures against anyone who published or made a statement or contributed to the insult and defamation of me, regardless of their position or status, whether they are an individual, an institution, or a sports entity.'.

Omani sports journalist Issa Stated, who covers Asian competitions, also came to Hattab's defence and insisted the claim the official was drunk is false.

'What happened to him was due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus,' he wrote on social media,.

'He underwent a medical examination after the match and was not intoxicated, contrary to what has been circulating.'.

The Syrian Football Federation added in a statement: 'Following an assessment of his health, it has been confirmed - contrary to various claims circulating on social media- that the reports regarding his situation are entirely unfounded.

'The Committee reiterates its unwavering support for him and is committed to thoroughly investigating all details and circumstances surrounding the incident.

'In this regard, the Committee has contacted the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) to request the referee’s medical report, the match commissioner’s report, and the referee assessor’s report, in order to accurately ascertain the facts of the incident and take the necessary follow-up actions.'.

Mauricio Pochettino was proud of Manchester United’s performance and his players’ early progress in the action-packed 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

The former Argentina international began his reign with a chastening 4-0 loss at rivals Liverpool on Sunday, when Leny Yoro’s early – and subsequently overturned – red card was the catalyst for Anfield agony.

More frustration followed on Wednesday, when Senne Lammens gifted Sporting a penalty converted by Luis Suarez shortly after denying him from the spot before Bruno Fernandes’ double with the help of a bobble put United in front.

But Suarez would level in the second half after nudging Lammens when attempting to gather a high ball and Pochettino’s hopes of a first win ended when home goalkeeper Kaique Pereira’s own goal was ruled out.

Szymon Marciniak adjudged Patrick Dorgu to have fouled him having been sent to the monitor on a night when the referee’s early whistle meant a disallowed first half Amad Diallo goal could not be overturned.

Youri Tielemans was incorrectly booked for his role in that incident and picked up a second booking at the end of an eventful night that saw Pochettino focus on the positives in Portugal.

Recent findings suggest that “I am so proud of our players, my players,” Pochettino told TNT Sports. “It was a really tough game.

“I like the team during 90 minutes, the personality, the character. And it’s true that it’s difficult to find some game that (you will) be more punished.

“We were punished a lot in different actions that were key, but I think everyone that watched the game saw all the action.

It has been revealed that “Only what I can say is I feel proud about the players. I think we today indicated the way that we want to play. It’s only one week working together. I feel so proud. I told them after the game.”.

Referee Marciniak’s poor performance will dominate the fallout to the draw at the Estadio Jose Alvalade, as will goalkeeper Lammens’ latest shaky display in a season replete with individual errors by United players.

Recent findings suggest that “Always we need to do double effort,” Pochettino stated. “We need to concentrate more and focus more and try to (do) recovery better, do all the effort.

“I think in this type of situation we start to fix also with results, but with (a) performance like today that is for me is the best medicine to prepare the next game.”.

Pochettino’s frantic start to life in charge continues on Saturday afternoon at Old Trafford, where he will take charge of United for the first time against Brentford.

The embattled Red Devils have just one win to show from their opening 11 Premier League matches and languish 19th in the standings.

Recent findings suggest that “I think we need to encourage and we need to really believe in our play,” Pochettino added. “We need to believe more and more and more.

“I think we need to give the capacity and the tools to perform and of course improving things.

“But that is the way that we need to show our aggression, like in the second half. We recover a lot of ball in the opposite half.

“We were aggressive, and I think I think that is the way that we want to play.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Representatives of Serbia's student-led movement were sworn in as lawmakers on Tuesday, just over four weeks after they ended Serbia's strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic's 14 years of rule.

The Students' List candidates officially took their seats in the inaugural parliamentary session as the first step for the youth-backed party toward forming Serbia's upcoming government.

The movement holds 140 seats in the 250-member parliament while Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) holds 103. The remaining seats belong to ethnic minority parties.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Hundreds gathered outside the parliament building in the capital Belgrade, to show their support for the student-backed lawmakers, most of whom are teachers, professors and other professionals with little or no political experience.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, SNS candidates were met with a negative reaction from the crowd. A woman in the crowd poured yogurt over an SNS member's head as she climbed the steps to the parliament entrance.

According to Serbian media, the newly elected lawmakers have been preparing for their first session for days. They will face veteran opposition politicians, including Aleksandar Vucic, who became the opposition leader after his defeat.

The Students' List will have 90 days to name a prime minister, present their programme and form a government, once the parliament is formed.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that the movement unites left- and right-wingers, pro-European and pro-Russian forces. It is focused on making changes in domestic politics and wants to advance European Union accession talks by implementing real reforms. The List opposes sanctions on Russia and the recognition of Kosovo — positions that almost the entire population of Serbia agrees with.

They pledged to improve healthcare, boost education and double the defense budget, along with many other reforms.

The election of a new parliamentary speaker will also lead to the appointment of a new acting president. The speaker has held the role since Vucic resigned in September to run for prime minister.

A snap presidential election must be called by November 27 and held by December 27.

Both parties are expected to put forward presidential candidates, but Vucic cannot seek another term because the constitution limits presidents to two terms in office.

Emery’s run without a win has extended to six matches in all competitions and Villa’s Champions League campaign does not promise to get any easier, with Paris St-Germain up next.

There was always likely to be a period of transition this season, as six of the heroes from the Europa League final’s starting XI were sold over the summer.

Despite some encouraging signs before the last international break, and three successive Champions League wins, Villa are now enduring a difficult run.

Their second-half performance in particular was poor, and Galatasaray secured victory with the evening’s first shot on target.

Aston Villa supporters have happy memories of Istanbul after May’s Europa League final, and they return to face Galatasaray this evening in a fixture which could forecast their Champions League prospects.

It has been par for the course for Unai Emery’s team in Europe so far, with victories over Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking and a defeat at Barcelona aligning with the form book.

Nine points from 12 leaves them inside the top eight at the halfway stage of the league phase, but tougher challenges are ahead with PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come after tonight’s game.

Recent findings suggest that since a statement victory over Manchester City, it has been a frustrating time for Villa either side of the international break. They were dumped out of the League Cup by Bournemouth, were second-best in a home draw with Fulham, threw away a pair of two-goal leads at Old Trafford, and were held by Sunderland at the weekend.

Though Villa put six past Galatasaray’s city rivals Fenerbahce at Villa Park, away games against Turkish opposition can be different beasts, as Liverpool discovered in the last round of Champions League matches.

Galatasaray’s two major attacking threats, Victor Osimhen and Rafael Leão, are both absent with injuries. Davinson Sanchez and Lucas Torreira are former Premier League players in their squad. Galatasaray have won two of four Champions League games, losing to Barcelona and Sporting Lisbon, but they are top of the Turkish Super Lig.

Villa will be without right-back Matty Cash owing to a concussion sustained during the international break with Poland, but will hope to have Victor Lindelof available again after he missed the Sunderland draw with illness.

Emery’s team were unable to train at Rams Park yesterday in order to give a troublesome pitch maximum recovery time after emergency renovation work.

In a recent development, “If we could have trained in the stadium of Galatasaray, maybe we would have decided for the same situation, but it’s not changing our routine,” Emery noted. “How the pitch is going to be tomorrow is important, but it’s not an excuse because it’s [the same] for both teams. Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible.”.

Tottenham Hotspur are resurgent in the Premier League – but that hasn't stopped one player's agent from linking his client with a move out of N17.

FourFourTwo understands that Spurs don't expect to do very much business in the winter window, with the likes of Jan Paul van Hecke, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio and Omar Marmoush signed over the summer in a £400 million spree that saw Tottenham smash their transfer record twice.

But while the summer saw significant departures, there could well be more where that came from this January, with one star publicly angling to leave.

The Lilywhites have won four of their last five fixtures in the league and turned their form around, as they look to bounce back from back-to-back 17th-placed finishes.

With plenty of interest in Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney from the likes of Manchester United and Newcastle, however, Spurs could see an opportunity to move on a wantaway fringe player from their squad.

Sport Witness have relayed an interview from Al-Maidan with Richarlison’s agent, Fidel Carvalho Soares, in which the Brazilian has been mentioned as a target for the Saudi Pro League.

Richarlison came close to an exit over the summer from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium but after the transfer fell through, he hasn't played under manager Roberto De Zerbi this term, with his future at the club to be decided in January.

“What is being said about negotiations between Al-Ahli and the player are just rumours,” Soares said, “However, Richarlison would welcome the opportunity to play in the Saudi league soon.

It has been revealed that “Richarlison really likes the idea of moving to Saudi Arabia, but there has been no contact from any clubs so far. These are just rumours. We are waiting for official offers, and at that point, we will explore the possibility of Richarlison’s transfer.”.

The agent added that Trabzonspor made an official offer over the summer but after the North Londoners rejected the bid, the Turkish side haven't been in contact again to rekindle the embers of a move.

The 29-year-old joined Spurs in 2022 in a deal that The Guardian reported as being worth £60 million at the time, after a successful 2021/22 season in which his 10 goals helped keep Everton in the Premier League.

Despite hitting double figures in the league twice in the capital, however, the forward has struggled for consistency and was omitted from Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil squad for the 2026 World Cup after leading the line for the Selecao at the last edition of the competition in Qatar four years earlier.

Richarlison is worth €15 million, according to Transfermarkt. Spurs travel to Sunderland this weekend when Premier League action resumes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia on Tuesday said it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee.

This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week over extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market.

The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable organization in the space of a month.

It has been revealed that since Huang's resignation, some investors — including Elon Musk and Donald Trump — have voiced concern that his departure could leave Nvidia and America's AI sector in peril and are now calling for his return. Huang on Tuesday, expressed regret for "serious mistakes" in his personal life before declaring he would be "honored" to return if the company's board of directors thought that was "in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.".

Nvidia is calling the fresh group its National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.

Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chair at Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee, joined by fellow directors Stephen Neal, a former CEO of a law firm, John Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).

According to recent reports, the committee will meet at least once every quarter. It will also incorporate independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts.

Nvidia already has a lower-level National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team; these groups will report to the board-level committee.

"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Board Chair Harvey Jones mentioned in a statement.

The company did not explicitly link the decision to November's developments and Huang's rapid fall from grace, but the timing seemed conspicuous.

The decision was announced hours ahead of Nvidia publishing its third-quarter results, with its still-stratospheric share price having fallen roughly 28% in the past month.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump, whom Huang was influential in persuading to allow the export of better-quality Nvidia chips to China than other US companies and officials deemed prudent, welcomed Nvidia's move on arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday.

Recent findings suggest that "Yes, that's a good idea. It's a great manufacturer," he said during a photo opportunity at a Manila meeting with the other "Quad" leaders from Australia, India and Japan. "It's a great idea.".

Trump reportedly owned Nvidia stock worth tens of millions of dollars before the share price fell. He also owns shares in other major tech companies.

According to recent reports, huang resigned last week after admitting to extramarital affairs in a message to Nvidia employees. This followed widespread reports, seemingly based on US and other intelligence, that one of the affairs was with a woman who used to lead a Singapore-based cloud computing company.

That tech giant, Megaspseed International, is a major Nvidia client and is suspected of diverting advanced chips to China in violation of US export controls. Intelligence officials also suspect Huang's partner of being an asset of Chinese intelligence services.

The reporting on the case also seems to show these suspicions had been known to US officials and other countries, including Singapore, for roughly a year.

The remains of a long-dead volcano on Mars | Space photo of the day for Nov. 23, 2026

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (468 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet.
  • The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible latest imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus.
  • This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet.

The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible latest imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus.

This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera.

Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains.

According to recent reports, despite its impressive height, it's still only about a medium-sized volcano for Mars, which is home much more impressively-sized volcanoes. For example, the planet's largest volcano Olympus Mons measures in at roughly 13.2 miles high (21.3 kilometers).

Industry observers note that while Tharsis Tholus might not be the tallest volcano on Mars, it is incredibly steep. It is steeper than Mauna Kea in Hawaii on Earth. To fully showcase the volcano's structure and topography in 3D, researchers actually exaggerated the vertical scale in this image, ESA reported.

It has been revealed that in addition to being steep and fairly tall, the volcano also has an interesting history. You can see that it is speckled with what look like small holes which are actually craters created by impacts from objects like asteroids. The volcano's current, unique shape is a combined effort by these impacts, environmental factors causing erosion and warping and ancient lava flows that left behind built-up material.

The observations by Mars Express also reveals cracks and other imperfections in the volcano. All of these details might seem like superficial bits of detail, however every small crater, every lumpy cliffside and every worn down surface hides information about the planet's past.

According to recent reports, by studying features like volcanoes on Mars, researchers can piece together what the planet may have looked like in its ancient past. How active was this volcano? How did it interact with the landscape around it? Observations like this can hold the answers.

Andoni Iraola has provided an update on Victor Munoz after the winger was forced off injured in Liverpool’s 3-0 win over Club Brugge.

The only downside on a night the Reds they kept their first clean sheet in the Champions League this season, Munoz took a heavy blow to the knee and was replaced by Rio Ngumoha in the 42nd minute.

The Spaniard, who scored his third Premier League goal in the routing of Manchester United on the weekend, was in visible agony as he was being treated but Iraola has revealed that the pain had subsided by the end of the match.

It has been revealed that “He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game has finished,” mentioned Iraola.

“It has been a knock on the knee so now we have to see how it presents tomorrow and see if it is just a knock – but it is very early to tell if there is something more.

“In the moment it was very painful and after the game I talked to him and he was more optimistic.”.

Iraola was nevertheless delighted with his two £100m men Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz as the pair’s goals edged Liverpool closer to Champions League qualification..

Isak scored at either end of the game to take his tally to 10 for the season – on target in his last six away games – with Wirtz continuing his good form with a sixth in five games for club and country.

Victory lifted Liverpool into fifth place on 12 points – in the two seasons of the new format, 16 has been enough to guarantee the top-eight finish needed to avoid a two-legged play-off in February.

In a recent development, “I am very pleased with the result and the performance overall. The result, 3-0, you can think it was an easy game but I don’t think it was,” mentioned Iraola.

Industry observers note that on Isak, he added: “Obviously he is in a great moment right now. In the first half especially he helped us a lot in the link-up, we were finding him very easily.

“The way they pressed was very aggressive and you have to find the last line straight away. Alex was helping us a lot in those situations.

Industry observers note that “In the second half it was more about defending a little bit lower. We knew they would push forward and give spaces to exploit.

“Sometimes they were leaving him one-v-one against the centre-backs and in one of those moments he has killed the game.”.

Isak said he was “in a good place…hopefully it gets better from here”.

He added on TNT sports: “The attack in general is beginning to click. We have a lot of different combinations and whoever comes in we have a dangerous attack. It feels good.”.

Isak and Wirtz are starting to form a profitable partnership, but Iraola believes the overall team performances are helping them flourish.

It has been revealed that “Both are now in a good place,” he said. “When the team overall is playing well and we are getting good results, everyone looks a little better. When everything collectively is not there, everyone looks a little bit worse.

Recent findings suggest that “The key part is they help the team to play well, to win games, to get results, and if we play well then we have chances, we are solid, everyone will play their part and will look better. Alex and Flo right now are in a good moment.”.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against Turkey over the detention of human rights lawyer and elected lawmaker Can Atalay.
  • The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.
  • The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against Turkey over the detention of human rights lawyer and elected lawmaker Can Atalay.

The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.

The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.

It ordered Turkey to pay him €32,500 (about $35,700) in compensation.

The judges stressed that Atalay's case should not be considered separately, but rather in the wider context of the detention of political opponents, human rights activists and journalists in Turkey.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Turkey was among the original signatories of the European Convention on Human Rights. Yet it has previously refused to comply with the court's decisions in the cases of rights activist Osman Kavala and prominent Kurdish politician Selahattin Demirtas.

As a lawyer, Atalay represented victims in numerous social and political cases in Turkey, as well as in freedom of speech cases involving journalists and writers.

He was also among the leading voices in the 2013 Gezi protests, which the government called an attempted coup.

Because of his involvement in the protests, Atalay, along with seven others, was sentenced to 18 years in prison in April 2022 for "aiding and abetting an attempted coup.".

Continuing his struggle from the infamous Silivri prison, Atalay ran as a candidate for the Workers' Party of Turkey (TIP) in the 2023 parliamentary elections.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A candidate for the earthquake-hit province of Hatay, he won his seat but was denied release despite multiple rulings by the Constitutional Court, Turkey's top court.

Recent findings suggest that his parliamentary status was revoked in 2024, a decision the Constitutional Court later overturned. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's party stopped the opposition from formally reading the decision in parliament.

Although a year later an opposition lawmaker read the decision in parliament, Atalay remains in jail.

After the ECHR's ruling was published, TIP leader Erkan Bas took to social media to call for Atalay's release and the restoration of his parliamentary mandate.

Darren Bent's beach ball bedlam, Nani's controversial quick-thinking and Peter Enckelman's calamitous mishap: Our experts pick the strangest goals they have ever seen after Bruno Fernandes' 'divot strike' in Lisbon

💡 Key Takeaways
